name: Django
covers: Rerail's own Django rules, from the Django docs and maintainers' review advice, for safe and efficient models, querysets, transactions, views and settings.

rules.title: Django practice: an inline queryset counted, loaded or truth-tested only to learn whether it has rows
Django practice: `len()` of an inline queryset whose rows are thrown away
Django practice: `<obj>.<fk>.id` or `.pk` where the row already holds `<fk>_id`
Django practice: a loop over an inline queryset that reads a relation of every row
Django practice: one create, save or get query per loop iteration
Django practice: a queryset bulk write on a model whose save()/delete() override or pre/post_save receiver it skips
Django practice: a numeric field read into Python, changed and saved back instead of updated with `F()`

caught.text:
from django.db import models


class Article(models.Model):
    hits = models.IntegerField(default=0)


def read(pk):
    a = Article.objects.get(pk=pk)
    a.hits += 1
    a.save()

rules.title: Django practice: `get_or_create()`/`update_or_create()` whose lookup no unique field or constraint covers
Django practice: a database error caught inside atomic, around queries with no savepoint of their own
Django practice: a `select_for_update()` in a function that a caller chain or a framework runs with no transaction open

passes.text:
from celery import shared_task
from django.db import transaction

from shop.models import Hold


@shared_task
def expire(pk):
    with transaction.atomic():
        hold = Hold.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=pk)
        hold.delete()

rules.title: Django practice: a task enqueued or a mail sent inside `transaction.atomic`
Django practice: a task enqueued or a mail sent from a view, or code it calls, while ATOMIC_REQUESTS wraps the request in a transaction
Django practice: a model instance passed as an argument to a Celery task
Django practice: a model field default that calls uuid4, random, now and the like once, at import

caught.text:
import uuid

from django.db import models


class Invite(models.Model):
    key = models.UUIDField(default=uuid.uuid4())

passes.text:
import uuid

from django.db import models


class Invite(models.Model):
    key = models.UUIDField(default=uuid.uuid4)

rules.title: Django practice: a model `__init__` that reads a field or changes the calling signature
Django practice: a model `save()` that sets a field and forwards `**kwargs` without handling `update_fields`

caught.text:
from django.db import models
from django.utils.text import slugify


class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=80)
    slug = models.SlugField()

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.slug = slugify(self.title)
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)

rules.title: Django practice: non-lazy `gettext` called when the module is imported

caught.text:
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _

STATUS = [("draft", _("Draft"))]

passes.text:
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _

STATUS = [("draft", _("Draft"))]

rules.title: Django practice: a form `clean_<field>()` that can end without returning the cleaned value
Django practice: a `clean()` override on a ModelForm or model formset that never calls the parent's `clean()`
Django practice: a view decorator put on a method without `method_decorator`
Django practice: a GET/HEAD handler that writes rows, itself or through what it calls
Django practice: the Host or X-Forwarded-Host header read directly instead of `request.get_host()`
Django practice: middleware reading `response.content` without handling streaming responses
Django practice: a runtime write to `django.conf.settings`
Django practice: an import of the project's settings module instead of `django.conf.settings`
Django practice: `request.user` read inside `async def` instead of `await request.auser()`

passes.text:
from django.http import JsonResponse


async def profile(request):
    user = await request.auser()
    return JsonResponse({"ok": user.is_authenticated})

rules.title: Django practice: a blocking ORM query in an `async def`, written there or reached through the sync functions it calls
